rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses tabbat as loss and links the root to the earlier discussion of tabāb in Ghāfir.
rows.anchor: أي: خسرت، وتقدم تفسير هذه المادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hands stand metonymically for the whole person, since most actions are done with them; the wording moves from a part to the whole.
rows.anchor: وأسند الفعل إلى اليدين مجازا لأن أكثر الأفعال تزاول بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Initially, tabbat is a curse or prayer and tab reports its fulfillment; he then says the apparent reading makes both verbs prayers.
rows.anchor: وقوله: " تبت " دعاء، و " تب " إخبار، أي: قد وقع

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: His reading وقد تب supports taking the second verb as reporting that the curse came to pass.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة عبد الله " وقد تب " والظاهر أن كليهما دعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers open the hāʾ of Lahab, while Ibn Kathīr sukunizes it; one view treats both forms as dialect variants, like النهر and الشعر.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة " لهب " بفتح الهاء. وابن كثير بإسكانها. فقيل: لغتان بمعنى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains the altered vowel in the proper name by analogy with Shams ibn Mālik, whose name is said to have changed from fatḥa to ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " وهو من تغيير الأعلام كقوله: " شمس ابن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shams example need not involve a changed proper name: shams can be the plural form attested in a phrase about horses.
rows.anchor: وجوز الشيخ في " شمس " أن يكون منقولا من " شمس " الجمع من قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kunya Abū Lahab may allude to his flushed, inflamed cheeks, his eventual Hellfire, its greater fame, the status of a kunya, or the ugliness of his given name ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā.
rows.anchor: وكنى بذلك: إما لالتهاب وجنتيه، وكان مشرق الوجه أحمره، وإما لما يؤول

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He gives three reasons for using a kunya: it was famous, his given name was ugly, or he was destined for Hellfire.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر ثلاثة أجوبة: إما لشهرته بكنيته، وإما لقبح اسمه كما تقدم، وإما لأن مآله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that the kunya is less complete conflicts with the later claim that a kunya is more honorable and complete.
rows.anchor: انتهى. وهذا يقتضي أن الكنية أشرف وأكمل لا أنقص، وهو عكس قول تقدم آنفا.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: A reading puts Abū in the nominative to preserve the name unchanged, as in familiar names and a reported distinction between two men named ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: وقرئ: " يدا أبو لهب " بالواو في مكان الجر. قال الزمخشري:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers agree on fatḥa in dhāta lahab; leaving the ending open preserves the rhyme pattern.
rows.anchor: ولم يختلف القراء في قوله: { ذات لهب } أنها بالفتح. والفرق أنها فاصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā in mā aghnā can be negation or an interrogative object; the interrogative is fronted because it has clause-initial position.
rows.anchor: يجوز في " ما " النفي والاستفهام، وعلى الثاني تكون منصوبة المحل بما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā kasaba can be a relative pronoun with its referent omitted, a verbal noun meaning his earning, or an interrogative meaning he gained nothing.
rows.anchor: يجوز في " ما " هذه أن تكون بمعنى الذي، فالعائد محذوف، وأن تكون مصدرية

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: He takes the interrogative reading of mā kasaba as rhetorically equivalent to a negation: what did he earn? Nothing.
rows.anchor: يعني: وأي شيء كسب؟ أي: لم يكسب شيئا، قاله الشيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating mā as directly negative is possible on that sense, but the author finds it unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يجوز أن تكون نافية، ويكون المعنى على ما ذكر، وهو غير ظاهر

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: His reading replaces kasaba with اكتسب.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: " وما اكتسب "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has fatḥa on yāʾ, a still ṣād, and an ungeminated lām, meaning that he enters the fire himself.
rows.anchor: العامة على فتح الياء وإسكان الصاد وتخفيف اللام، أي: يصلى هو بنفسه

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Muqsam, and ʿAbbās in his selected reading use ḍamma on yāʾ, fatḥa on ṣād, and a doubled lām.
rows.anchor: وأبو حيوة وابن مقسم وعباس في اختياره بالضم والفتح والتشديد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read with ḍamma on yāʾ and sukūn on ṣād.
rows.anchor: والحسن وأبن أبي إسحاق بالضم والسكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common nominative makes wife and ḥammālat al-ḥaṭab a subject-predicate sentence; alternatively the wife coordinates with the pronoun in سيصلى, licensed by the intervening object.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة بالرفع على أنهما جملة من مبتدأ وخبر سيقت للإخبار بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If wife coordinates with the pronoun in سيصلى, ḥammālat can be her adjective, explanatory apposition, substitute, or predicate of an omitted هي.
rows.anchor: و " حمالة الحطب " على هذا فيه أوجه: كونها نعتا ل " امرأته ".

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the word for wife in diminutive forms, sometimes retaining the hamza and sometimes replacing it with yāʾ and assimilating it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس " ومريته " و " مريئته " على التصغير، إلا أنه أقر الهمزة تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has ḥammālat nominative, while ʿĀṣim reads it accusative as an insult, glossed by al-Zamakhsharī as a pointed slur against Umm Jamīl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة { حمالة } بالرفع. وعاصم بالنصب فقيل: على الشتم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He understands the accusative as a slur: it is an apt epithet for the woman known as Umm Jamīl.
rows.anchor: قاله الزمخشري، وكانت تكنى بأم جميل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative may instead be a circumstantial accusative from the wife if she coordinates with the pronoun in سيصلى; deriving it from a pronoun inside the later prepositional phrase is weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نصب على الحال من " أمرأته " إذا جعلناها مرفوعة بالعطف على الضمير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some object that a definite construct describing past activity cannot be a circumstantial accusative; the reply is that the sense is future, as she carries firewood in a bundle in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ثم أجاب بأن المراد الاستقبال لأنه ورد في التفسير: أنها تحمل يوم القيامة حزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes her carrying firewood literally; another makes it a metaphor for gossip and stirring conflict among people.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: { حمالة الحطب } قولان. أحدهما: هو حقيقة. والثاني: أنه مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poet uses ḥammālū al-ḥaṭab for tale-bearers, witnessing the metaphorical sense.
rows.anchor: إن بني الأدرم حمالو الحطب هم الوشاة في الرضا وفي الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another anonymous poem describes walking among people with moist firewood, whose dampness reinforces the metaphor.
rows.anchor: ولم تمش بين الحي بالحطب الرطب جعله رطبا تنبيها على تدخينه

rows.speaker: أبو قلابة
rows.claim: Abū Qilāba reads ḥāmilat, a form that can also carry the common reading's meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو قلابة { حاملة الحطب } على وزن فاعلة. وهي محتملة

rows.speaker: عباس
rows.claim: ʿAbbās reads ḥammālata li-l-ḥaṭab with tanwīn and a redundant strengthening lām before the object, comparable to Hūd 11:107.
rows.anchor: وعباس " حمالة للحطب " بالتنوين وجر المفعول بلام زائدة تقوية للعامل،

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: In one transmission, Abū ʿAmr lightly shortens the final hāʾ instead of fully pronouncing it.
rows.anchor: وأبو عمرو في رواية " وامرأته " باختلاس الهاء دون إشباع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one parse, fī jīdihā is the predicate of the wife and ḥabl its subject; it may instead be circumstantial, or a fronted predicate with ḥabl as delayed subject.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " في جيدها " خبرا ل " امرأته " و " حبل " فاعل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jīd means neck and its plural is ajyād; Imruʾ al-Qays uses it in a simile.
rows.anchor: والجيد: العنق، ويجمع على أجياد. قال امرؤ القيس:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad can mean palm-fiber rope, fiber generally, or the bark of a Yemeni tree.
rows.anchor: والمسد: ليف المقل: وقيل: الليف مطلقا. وقيل: هو لحاء شجر باليمن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse uses masad; the word can also refer to ropes made from camel hides or hair.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة: 4673 مقذوفة بدخيس النحض بازلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed verse also attests masad from camels, and a man described as mamṣūd in build is strongly made.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون من جلود الإبل وأوبارها. وأنشد: 4647 ومسد أمر من أيانق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If huwa refers to the situation implied by reports that people asked the Prophet to describe God's lineage or whether He was copper or iron, Allah can be the subject and aḥad its predicate.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه ضمير عائد على ما يفهم من السياق، فإنه يروى في الأسباب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that contextual reading, Allah may instead be apposition, a first predicate followed by aḥad as second predicate, or aḥad may predicate an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " الله " بدلا، و " أحد " الخبر. ويجوز أن يكون " الله " خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively huwa is the pronoun of the matter, an honorific construction whose following sentence explains it.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه ضمير الشأن لأنه موضع تعظيم، والجلمة بعده خبره مفسرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known analysis derives the hamza of aḥad from wāw in waḥda; unlike generic aḥad, its hamza is not original, though Abū al-Baqāʾ reports the contrary.
rows.anchor: وهمزة " أحد " بدل من واو، لأنه من الوحدة، وإبدال الهمزة من الواو المفتوحة.

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: Thaʿlab distinguishes wāḥid, which accepts counting, duals, and plurals, from aḥad, which does not.
rows.anchor: وفرق ثعلب بين " واحد " وبين " أحد " بأن الواحد يدخله العد والجمع والاثنان

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: He says one may call God aḥad but not Zayd, because this exclusivity belongs to God whereas Zayd has changing states.
rows.anchor: ويقال: الله أحد، ولا يقال: زيد أحد؛ لأن لله تعالى هذه الخصوصية

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh rebuts Thaʿlab by pointing out that aḥad occurs within numbers such as twenty-one.
rows.anchor: ورد عليه الشيخ: بأنه يقال: أحد وعشرون ونحوه فقد دخله العدد

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī derives aḥad from waḥad, with wāw changed to hamza and one of the resulting adjacent alifs deleted for ease.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي: " إن أحدا أصله وأحد، فأبدلت الواو همزة فاجتمع ألفان

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy read Allah aḥad without qul; a reading attributed to the Prophet has only aḥad, and al-Aʿmash reads al-wāḥid.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبي { الله أحد } دون " قل " وقرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم " أحد "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanwīn on aḥad is the standard form; a large group of named readers omit it at a word junction to avoid two adjacent sukūns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة بتنوين " أحد " وهو الأصل. وزيد بن علي وأبان ابن عثمان وابن أبي إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation gives anonymous poetic evidence for omitting tanwīn at a junction: one line ends with رجال مكة مسنتون عجاف.
rows.anchor: ورجال مكة مسنتون عجاف وقال آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous poetic example ends ولا ذاكر الله إلا قليلا and supports the same connected pronunciation.
rows.anchor: فألفيته غير مستعتب ولا ذاكر الله إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣamad is an active-form word with passive meaning: the master to whom needs are directed and whom alone can fulfill them.
rows.anchor: فعل بمعنى مفعول كالقبض والنقض. وهو السيد الذي يصمد إليه في الحوائج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poem calls ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd the master al-ṣamad, illustrating the sense of a preeminent master.
rows.anchor: بعمرو بن مسعود وبالسيد الصمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another poem addresses a man as al-sayyid al-ṣamad, again using it for a master.
rows.anchor: خذها حذيف فأنت السيد الصمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported meaning is one without an interior cavity, supported by a poem describing a battle-ready horse.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الصمد: هو الذي لا جوف له، ومنه قوله: 4679 شهاب حروب لا تزال جياده

rows.speaker: ابن كعب
rows.claim: Ibn Kaʿb takes al-ṣamad as explained by the following statement that God neither begets nor is begotten.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كعب: تفسيره ما بعده من قوله: " لم يلد ولم يولد "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers al-ṣamad to stand as an independent informative clause; making it an adjective with the next clause as predicate is weak because each clause is independently informative.
rows.anchor: والأحسن في هذه الجملة أن تكون مستقلة بفائدة هذا الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes aḥad the subject of yakun, kafu its predicate, and lahu dependent on kafu; this is used in a debate over fronted adverbs.
rows.anchor: " أحد " اسمها و " له " متعلق بالخبر، اي: ولم يكن أحد كفوا له.

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad uses the verse against Sībawayh's view that a fronted adverb should be the predicate.
rows.anchor: وقد رد المبرد على سيبويه بهذه الآية، من حيث إنه يزعم أنه إذا تقدم الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is that Sībawayh only allowed that analysis, not required it; another analysis makes the adverb predicate and kafu a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن سيبويه لم يحتم ذلك بل جوزه. والثاني: أنا لا نسلم أن الظرف هنا ليس بخبر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says an ungoverned adverb normally comes later, but it is fronted here because negating any counterpart to God is the verse's focus.
rows.anchor: قلت: هذا الكلام إنما سيق لنفي المكافأة عن ذات الباري تعالى، وهذا المعنى مصبه

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Another parse makes kafu a circumstantial accusative from aḥad, which was originally its adjective, while lahu is the predicate.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن ينصب على الحال من " أحد " لأنه كان صفته فلما تقدم عليه نصب حالا

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: The circumstantial accusative may alternatively refer to the implicit pronoun inside the prepositional phrase when that phrase is taken as the predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حالا من الضمير المستكن في الجار لوقوعه خبرا

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh says lahu is incomplete and attaches to kafu, fronted for emphasis; on this account lahu cannot be the predicate and kafu a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ بعد أن حكى كلام الزمخشري ومكي: " وهذه الجملة ليست من هذا الباب وذلك

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: He says kafu intervenes before the delayed subject to emphasize the pronoun referring to God and to leave the final position to the subject as rhyme.
rows.anchor: وتقدم على " كفوا " للاهتمام به، إذ فيه ضمير الباري تعالى، وتوسط الخبر

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh says the delayed subject preserves the verse end rhyme.
rows.anchor: لأن تأخير الاسم هو فاصلة فحسن ذلك.

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh distinguishes adverbs that can function as predicates from those that cannot.
rows.anchor: وسيـبويه إنما تكلم في الظرف الذي يصلح أن يكون خبرا وأن لا يكون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that the adverb can carry useful predicative meaning, asking how it could otherwise make a complete clause with أحد.
rows.anchor: التقديم والتأخير والإلغاء والاستقرار عربي جيد كثير قال تعالى: { ولم يكن له كفوا أحد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on both k and f; other readers soften the hamza, sukunize f, or replace hamza with wāw in pause or throughout.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العامة بضم الكاف والفاء. وسهل الهمزة الأعرج وشيبة ونافع في رواية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulaymān ibn ʿAlī reads kifāʾ with kasra and lengthening, meaning a counterpart; al-Nābigha's verse attests the word.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سليمان بن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس " كفاء " بالكسر والمد، أي: لا مثل له.

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: In one transmission, Nāfiʿ reads kafā with kasra and fatḥa but no lengthening, as if he transferred the hamza's vowel and deleted it.
rows.anchor: ونافع في رواية " كفا " بالكسر وفتح الفاء من غير مد، كأنه نقل حركة الهمزة وحذفها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufʾ means an equivalent; saying this is your kufʾ means it is your counterpart, and the verbal noun is kafāʾa.
rows.anchor: والكفء: النظير. وهذا كفء لك، أي: نظيرك والاسم الكفاءة بالفتح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-falaq is dawn, a passive-form noun meaning that which is split open; a report compares a vision to dawn's break, and two poems attest the word.
rows.anchor: هو الصبح. وهو فعل بمعنى مفعول كالقبض، اي: مفلوق. وفي الحديث:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify al-falaq as a pit in Hell, a low place in the earth, or anything split open, such as seed or earth by vegetation; its plural is fulqān.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جب في جهنم. وقيل: المطمئن من الأرض. وجمعه فلقان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase min sharri mā khalaq attaches to aʿūdhu; the common reading makes sharri an annexation, while ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads it with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: متعلق ب " أعوذ " والعامة على إضافة " شر " إلى " ما " وقرأ عمرو بن فائد بتنوينه.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and some Muʿtazilites take mā as negative, reflecting their claim that God did not create evil.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " عمرو بن عبيد وبعض المعتزلة الذين يرون أن الله لم يخلق الشر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says mā need not be negative: it can be relative and appositional to sharri with an omitted annexation, first generalizing and then specifying.
rows.anchor: انتهى ولا يتعين أن تكون " ما " نافية، بل يجوز أن تكون موصولة بدلا من " شر " على حذف مضاف،

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows mā to be apposition to sharri or extra, but rejects a negative reading because a negative's scope cannot be preceded by material from within it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابو البقاء: " وما على هذا بدل من " شر " أو زائدة. ولا يجوز أن تكون نافية؛ لأن النافية لا يتقدم عليها ما في حيزها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Abū al-Baqāʾ's grammatical objection sound and says deleting the object of khalaqa would violate the normal construction.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول " خلق " لأنه خلاف الأصل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may also be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: [و " ما " مصدرية، أو بمعنى الذي].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqaba can describe night growing dark, punishment arriving, or the sun setting; a cited poem uses it for punishment falling on people.
rows.anchor: قوله: { وقب }: وقب الليل: أظلم، والعذاب: حل، والشمس:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghāsiq is interpreted as night or moon; night may be called ghāsiq because of its cold, and refuge is sought from its nighttime hazards.
rows.anchor: والغاسق قيل: الليل. وقيل: القمر. سمي الليل غاسقا لبرودته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poem uses ghasiqa for the night becoming dark and dense.
rows.anchor: إذ جئتنا طارقا والليل قد غسقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is an adverb attached to aʿūdhu, specifying the time at which refuge is sought.
rows.anchor: و " إذا " منصوب ب " أعوذ " ، أي: أعوذ بالله من هذا في وقت كذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naffāthāt is an intensive plural from nafatha, to blow; Abū al-Faḍl distinguishes breath without saliva from tafl with saliva.
rows.anchor: من نفث، أي: نفخ. واختلف فيه فقال أبو الفضل: شبه النفخ من الفم

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل
rows.claim: Abū al-Faḍl cites an anonymous poem in which the speaker says he did not nafatha on someone, evidencing the sense of a puff in incantation.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان بريق فهو التفل وأنشد: 4686 فإن يبرأ فلم أنفث عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead defines نفث as a blow accompanied by saliva.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " نفخ معه ريق "

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads al-naffāthāt with ḍamma on the initial nūn, a noun comparable to al-naffākha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن " النفاثات " بضم النون، وهي اسم كالنفاخة.

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Qāsim read al-nāfithāt, a form compatible with the common reading.
rows.anchor: ويعقوب وعبد الله بن القاسم " النافثات " وهي محتملة لقراءة العامة،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Abū al-Rabīʿ also read al-nafathāt without the alif, like ḥādhir and ḥadhir.
rows.anchor: والحسن ايضا وأبو الربيع " النفثات " دون ألف كحاذر وحذر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāsiq and ḥāsid are indefinite because their harm may fail to occur, so indefiniteness conveys partiality; al-naffāthāt is definite either by prior mention in tafsir or to intensify the evil.
rows.anchor: ونكر غاسقا وحاسدا لأنه قد يتخلف الضرر فيهما. فالتنكير يفيد التبعيض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik al-nās and ilāh al-nās can be adjectives of Rabb al-nās, appositions, or explanatory apposition.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكونا وصفين ل " رب الناس " وأن يكونا بدلين، وأن يكونا عطف بيان.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers explanatory apposition: Rabb can be used of false lords, Malik may also be shared, while Ilāh is exclusive to God and completes the specification.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان كقولك: سيرة أبي حفص عمر الفاروق، بين بملك الناس، ثم زيد بيانا؛

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The shaykh objects that explanatory apposition is normally expressed by substantives; the reply is that these descriptions function like substantives here.
rows.anchor: واعترض الشيخ بأن البيان بالجوامد. ويجاب عنه: بأن هذا جار مجرى الجوامد.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains Rabb al-nās as the one who owns their affairs, since refuge is sought from the whisperer who whispers in people's hearts.
rows.anchor: لأن الاستعاذة وقعت من شر الموسوس في صدور الناس فكأنه قيل: أعوذ من شر الموسوس إلى الناس بربهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains repeating al-nās as appropriate because explanatory apposition tends to repeat the expressed noun.
rows.anchor: لأن عطف البيان فكان مظنة للإظهار

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls waswās a noun meaning whispering, like zalzāl for zalzala; the closed-vowel form is the verbal noun, and the devil is named for his work or as its possessor.
rows.anchor: اسم بمعنى الوسوسة كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة، وأما المصدر فوسواس بالكسر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author refers back to his earlier discussion distinguishing the verbal noun with kasra from the noun with fatḥa in the parallel word zalzala.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى الكلام معه في أن المكسور مصدر، والمفتوح اسم في الزلزلة فليراجع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khannās means one who repeatedly retreats; the devil withdraws when God is remembered.
rows.anchor: قوله { الخناس } ، أي: الرجاع، لأنه إذا ذكر الله تعالى خنس وهو مثال مبالغة من الخنوس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī may be genitive as an adjective, substitute, or explanatory apposition; it may also be cut off in the accusative or nominative.
rows.anchor: قوله: { الذى يوسوس }: يجوز جره نعتا وبدلا وبيانا لجريانه مجرى الجوامد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-jinnah may be a renewed-preposition apposition to sharr, or apposition to the possessor of waswās, since whisperers include jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: فيه أوجه، أحدها: أنه بدل من " شر " بإعادة العامل، أي: من شر الجنة. الثاني: أنه بدل من ذي الوسواس؛ لأن الموسوس من الجن والإنس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can be a circumstantial phrase describing the subject of yuwaswisu, or apposition to al-nās with min serving to explain the two kinds.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه حال من الضمير في " يوسوس " أي: يوسوس حال كونه من هذين الجنسين. الرابع: أنه بدل من " الناس "

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says jinn are called nās because they move about in pursuing their aims.
rows.anchor: وأطلق على الجن اسم الناس؛ لأنهم يتحركون في مراداتهم، قاله أبو البقاء.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects calling jinn people: jinn are hidden by definition, whereas nās and bashar are visible; he cites verses calling jinn nafar and rijāl.
rows.anchor: ما أحقه؛ لأن الجن سموا جنا لاجتنانهم والناس ناسا لظهورهم، من الإيناس وهو الإبصار،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He suggests instead that al-nās could mean the forgetful, as in the verse يوم يدع الداع, and the phrase من حيث أفاض الناسي; the author says the latter uses a kasra in place of yāʾ for the active participle.
rows.anchor: وكما قرئ { من حيث أفاض الناسي } ثم بين بالجنة والناس؛ لأن الثقلين هما النوعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth parse makes the phrase explain the whisperer, since there are human and jinn devils; Qur'an 6:112 names devils of both kinds, and Abū Dharr asked about seeking refuge from human devils.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أنه بيان للذي يوسوس، على أن الشيطان ضربان: إنسي وجني، كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth parse attaches the phrase to yuwaswisu, with min marking the source: whispering comes from jinn and from humans.
rows.anchor: السادس: أنه يتعلق ب " يوسوس " و " من " لابتداء الغاية، أي: يوسوس في صدورهم من جهة الجن

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī makes al-nās coordinate with al-waswās, meaning refuge from whisperers and people; he rejects coordination with jinnah because people do not whisper into hearts, though the author says humans do whisper suitably.
rows.anchor: السابع: أن " والناس " عطف على " الوسواس " أي: من شر الوسواس والناس. ولا يجوز عطفه

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: A further parse takes wa-al-nās as coordinated with al-jinnah; Abū al-Baqāʾ also offers min al-jinnah as a circumstance of al-nās, but the author finds the circumstantial analyses semantically unsound and the explanation confused.
rows.anchor: الثامن: أن { من الجنة } حال من " الناس " ، أي: كائنين من القبيلين، قاله أبو البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's preferred overall reading takes the phrase as clarification that whisperers include both human and jinn devils, while people can whisper in a manner appropriate to them.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الناس يوسوسون أيضا بمعنى يليق بهم

none: closing authorial colophon and prayer only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabbih means to declare the Lord free of evil and to say subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā.
rows.anchor: أي نزه ربك عن السوء وقل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the human being in balanced form, made him testify that God is his Lord, and created him upon the natural disposition.
rows.anchor: خلق الإنسان مستويا، أشهده على نفسه بأنه ربه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the way, whether the person proves grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: هداه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians say the phrase means He guided and led astray, with led astray omitted because the context supplies it, as in 14:4.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: فهدى وأضل ولكن حذفت وأضل لأن في الكلام دليلا عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥwā is a circumstantial accusative modifying pasture: God brought it out green, tinged with dark hue, then dried it into brittle stubble like debris atop floodwater.
rows.anchor: أحوى أي أخرجه أخضر يضرب إلى الحوة، والحوة السواد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aflaha means attaining lasting life and bliss; tazakkā means growing through God-consciousness, and zakī means growing and abundant.
rows.anchor: أي قد صادف البقاء الدائم والفوز بالنعيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading has second-person taʾ, supported by Ubayy's explanatory reading بل أنتم تؤثرون الحياة الدنيا; another reading has third-person yāʾ.
rows.anchor: والأجود التاء، لأنها رويت عن أبي بن كعب:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to the statements from verses 14 through 18; another view takes it as referring to the whole sura.
rows.anchor: يعني من قوله: (قد أفلح من تزكى) إلى هذا الموضع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghāshiyah is interpreted as the Resurrection, which covers creation, or Hell, which covers unbelievers' faces.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الغاشية القيامة لأنها تغشى الخلق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāshiʿah is the predicate of wujūh and means humbled or abased.
rows.anchor: (خاشعة) خبر (وجوه)، ومعنى خاشعة ذليلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀmilah nāṣibah may describe people who labored in worldly life for what does not draw them near to God, monks and similar people, or people laboring under punishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها عاملة ناصبة في الدنيا لغير ما يقرب إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has taṣlā with this vocalization.
rows.anchor:
(تصلى نارا حامية (4)
ويقرأ (تصلى).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āniyah means having reached extreme heat, comparable to ḥamīm ān in 44:46.
rows.anchor: أي متناهية في شدة الحر: كقوله: (يطوفون بينها وبين حميم آن (44).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns Hell's people: ḍarīʿ is shubruq, a thorny plant called shubruq when wet and ḍarīʿ when dry.
rows.anchor: يعني لأهل النار، والضريع الشبرق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh objected that ḍarīʿ fattens their camels; the response is that Hell's food neither nourishes nor relieves hunger.
rows.anchor: قال كفار قريش: إن الضريع لتسمن عليه إبلنا، فقال الله - عز وجل -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening asks whether the account had reached the Prophet and his people; such narratives were previously unknown to them, as in 11:49.
rows.anchor: ومعنى (هل أتاك) أي هذا ألم يكن من علمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse is read lā tusmaʿ and lā yasmaʿ; it can mean no offensive speech is heard, or no discarded talk is spoken, since the people speak only wisdom and praise.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (لا يسمع فيها لاغية)، وقرئت (لا تسمع فيها لاغية)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akwwāb are vessels resembling pitchers but without handles.
rows.anchor: الأكواب آنية شبيهة بالأباريق لا عرى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namāriq is the plural of nimriqah.
rows.anchor:
الأكواب آنية شبيهة بالأباريق لا عرى لها.
* * *
(ونمارق مصفوفة (15)
واحدتها نمرقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarābī are rugs, and the singular is zarabiyyah.
rows.anchor:
(وزرابي مبثوثة (16)
الذرابي: البسط، واحدتها زربية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God points to the remarkable camel: even a small child can lead and breed it; it rises while carrying a heavy load, unlike other beasts of burden, showing God's oneness.
rows.anchor: نبههم الله على عظيم من خلقه قد ذلله للصغير يقوده وينتجه وينهضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky was raised without pillars.
rows.anchor: يعني بغير عمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are planted firmly and do not move.
rows.anchor:
(وإلى الجبال كيف نصبت (19)
(نصبت) مرساة مثبتة لا تزول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was spread out and flattened.
rows.anchor: أي دحيت وبسطت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to remind came before the Prophet was ordered to fight.
rows.anchor: هذا قبل أن يؤمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالحرب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who exercises control or domination.
rows.anchor: أي بمسلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception concerns one who turns away and disbelieves; the greater punishment is Hell.
rows.anchor: أي عذاب جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyāb means return, as a verbal noun from āba; its original form iwyāban undergoes assimilation and vowel change.
rows.anchor: ومعنى إيابهم رجوعهم، ومعنى (إيابهم) على مصدر أيب إيابا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iyāb is read with a light or doubled yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرئت إيابهم، بالتخفيف والتثقيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fajr is dawn breaking out of night, and the oath's answer is that God watches in ambush.
rows.anchor: الفجر انفجار الصبح من الليل، وجواب القسم (إن ربك لبالمرصاد (14)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are the nights of Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
rows.anchor:
(وليال عشر (2)
ليالي عشر ذي الحجة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-watr with fatḥa can mean the day of sacrifice, while al-witr is the day of ʿArafah; other explanations take shafʿ and watr as even and odd numbers, or creation in pairs and God as the One.
rows.anchor: قرئت (والوتر) بفتح الواو، والوتر يوم النحر، والوتر يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasri means the night passed; deleting yāʾ marks an end rhyme and follows the muṣḥaf, though another reading retains it, and the common deletion is preferred.
rows.anchor:
إذا مضى. سرى يسري، كما قال - عز وجل:
(والليل إذ أدبر).
و (يسر) حذفت الياء لأنها رأس آية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the muṣḥaf's deletion of yāʾ because it is the more common reading; rhyme-final vowels signal the deletion.
rows.anchor:
واتباع المصحف وحذف الياء أحب إلي لأن القراءة بذلك أكثر.
ورووس الآي فواصل تحذف معها الياءات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God watches for those who disbelieve in Him and worship another, with punishment.
rows.anchor: أي يرصدا من كفر به وعبد غيره بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtalā means tested; God's favor and increase in provision lead the person to say that his Lord honored him.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إذا ما اختبره ربه وأوسع عليه فيقول ربي أكرمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrasting test consists in making one's provision measured or constrained, leading the person to say that God humiliated him.
rows.anchor: أي جعل رزقه مقدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā rejects the person's equation of worldly abundance with honor and poverty with humiliation; this is the unbeliever who denies resurrection, whereas the believer sees honor in success toward the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهذا يعنى به الكافر الذي لا يؤمن بالبعث، وإنما الكرامة عنده والهوان بكثرة الحظ في الدنيا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has lā taḥāḍḍūn; another has lā taḥāḍḍūna concerning urging food for the poor.
rows.anchor:
(ولا تحضون)
ويقرأ (ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They used to consume orphans' property greedily and hastily; the reprimand then says they fail to honor orphans and urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يأكلون أموال اليتامى إسرافا وبدارا فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-lamm means gathering together: they gather and consume all of the inherited property, specifically the orphans' inheritance.
rows.anchor: أي تراث اليتامى (لما) يلمون بجميعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When calling a woman, one may say yā ayyatuhā or yā ayyuhā; the former treats ayā as feminine, while the latter reflects its ambiguity and construction.
rows.anchor: " أي " تؤنث إذا دعوت بها مؤنثا وتذكر، تقول: يا أيتها المرأة.

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports that some Arabs say kullatuhunna for kulluhunna.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن بعض العرب تقول كلتهن في كلهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul is settled in faith and humbly devoted to its Lord.
rows.anchor: والمطمئنة التي اطمأنت بالإيمان وأخبتت إلى ربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marḍiyyah derives from the older form marḍwah; the soul is pleased with what God gives, approved, and purified.
rows.anchor: أصل (مرضية) مرضوة أي راضية بما أتاها، قد رضيت وزكيت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fadkhulī fī ʿibādī means entering among God's chosen servants.
rows.anchor: في جملة عبادي المصطفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has fī ʿabdī in the singular; on it, God may mean entering into the companion from whom the soul emerged.
rows.anchor:
وقرئت فادخلي في عبدي.
(وادخلي جنتي (30)
فعلى هذه القراءة - والله أعلم - ادخلي إلى صاحبك الذي خرجت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading and interpretation are fī ʿibādī followed by wadkhulī jannatī.
rows.anchor: والأكثر في القراءة والتفسير: (فادخلي في عبادي (29) وادخلي جنتي (30).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-balad refers to Mecca, and lā uqsimu means I swear; lā is added for emphasis.
rows.anchor:
يعنى بالبلد ههنا مكة، والمعنى أقسم بهذا البلد.
و" لا " أدخلت توكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has la-uqsimu, with the lām of oath and emphasis, but it is rare and linguistically strained because future oath-lām normally requires nūn; Sībawayh and al-Khalīl explain its use with anna.
rows.anchor:
وقرئت (لأقسم بهذا البلد).
تكون اللام لام القسم والتوكيد، وهذه القراءة قليلة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca was made lawful to the Prophet for one daytime hour, not to anyone before or after him, permitting hunting, cutting grass, and breaking branches.
rows.anchor: أحلت مكة للنبي عليه السلام ساعة من النهار، ولم تحل لأحد قبله ولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective ḥill has related forms ḥalāl and muḥill, contrasted with ḥarām, ḥurum, and muḥrim.
rows.anchor: يقال: رجل حل وحلال ومحل، وكذلك رجل حرام وحرم ومحرم (1).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also read without hamza and means shut or sealed; both āṣada and awṣada mean to close a door.
rows.anchor:
ويقرأ بغير همز، ومعناه مطبقة.
يقال آصدت الباب وأوصدته إذا أطبقته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says God taught the soul the paths of sin and guidance.
rows.anchor: قيل علمها طريق الفجور وطريق الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that inspiring the soul to piety means granting it success, while inspiring it to sin means abandoning it to failure.
rows.anchor: والكلام على أن ألهمها التقوى، وفقها للتقوى، وألهمها فجورها خذلها، والله أعلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aflaha describes the soul God purified; another view makes it a person who purifies himself by righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: أي قد أفلحت نفس زكاها الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dassa means God made the soul low and base; the root form is dassasah, with one repeated consonant changed to yāʾ when like letters accumulate.
rows.anchor: والأصل دسسها، ولكن الحروف إذا اجتمعت من لفظ واحد أبدل من أحدها ياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poetic line, تقضي البازي إذا البازي كسر, illustrates the same consonant pattern, with taqaḍḍa intended.
rows.anchor:
تقضي البازي إذا البازي كسر
قالوا معناه تقضض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭaghwā means tyranny and derives from ṭughyān; in a faʿlā noun from a root with yāʾ, yāʾ becomes wāw to distinguish noun from adjective, as in taqwā and khazyā.
rows.anchor:
أي بطغيانها، وأصل (طغواها) طغيها وفعلى إذا كانت من ذوات الياء
أبدلت في الاسم واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāqat Allāh is accusative with an implied leave or spare; the she-camel and her watering turn were to be left alone, since she had one day and they another.
rows.anchor: (ناقة) منصوب على معنى ذروا ناقة الله، كما قال سبحانه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They disbelieved the warning and did not believe punishment would come when told not to harm the she-camel.
rows.anchor: أي فلم يوقنوا أنهم يعذبون حين قال لهم (ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب يوم عظيم).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama means to cover or encompass with punishment; repeated application intensifies the covering, as in covering a grave or a camel coated in fat.
rows.anchor:
معناه دمدم عليهم أطبق عليهم العذاب، يقال: دمدمت على الشيء إذا
أطبقت عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority of tafsir takes the subject of not fearing consequences as God; other views make it Ṣāliḥ or the man who rose among them, the most wretched.
rows.anchor:
أكثر ما جاء في التفسير لا يخاف الله تعالى تبعة ما أنزل بهم، وقيل لا
يخاف رسول الله صالح عليه السلام الذي أرسل إليهم عقباها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍāll means the Prophet did not yet know the Qur'an or religious laws, so God guided him to them; 42:52 supports this explanation.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يكن يدري القرآن ولا الشرائع فهداه الله إلى القرآن وشرائع الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group says he remained upon his people's way for forty years.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: كان على أمر قومه أربعين سنة (1).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not oppress the orphan with respect to his property.
rows.anchor: أي لا تقهره على ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not scold the requester: either give him something or refuse him gently.
rows.anchor: أي لا تنهره، إما أعطيته، وإما رددته ردا لينا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tell the blessing by conveying the message and speaking of the prophethood God granted, the greatest blessing.
rows.anchor: أي بلغ ما أرسلت به وحدث بالنبوة التي آتاك الله وهي أجل النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct all longing and desire to God alone.
rows.anchor: أي اجعل رغبتك إلى الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir reports that اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق was the first Qur'anic verse revealed.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن أول آية نزلت من القرآن (اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught writing with the pen.
rows.anchor: أي الذي علم الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses were revealed concerning Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
rows.anchor:
هذه نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام، وكذلك: (أرأيت الذي ينهى (9) عبدا إذا صلى (10).
لأن أبا جهل قال: إن رأيت محمدا يصلي توطأت عنقه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lasfaʿ means to seize and drag forcefully, here dragging the forelock toward Hell.
rows.anchor:
أي لنجرن ناصيته إلى النار، يقال: سفعت بالشيء إذا اقبضت عليه
وجذبته جذبا شديدا (1).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lying, sinful forelock means its owner is a liar and sinner, like saying someone's day fasts and night prays.
rows.anchor:
وتأويله بناصية صاحبها كاذب خاطئ، كما يقال فلان نهاره صائم وليله
قائم، المعنى هو صائم في نهاره وقائم في ليله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His nādī means the people at his gathering or his clan, whom he is challenged to call for support.
rows.anchor: معناه فليدع أهل ناديه، وهم أهل مجلسه، وكانوا عشيرته أي فليستنصر بهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zabāniyah are severe, stern angels, as described in 66:6.
rows.anchor: الزبانية الغلاظ الشداد، واحدهم زبنية، وهم ههنا الملائكة، قال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā denies Abū Jahl's claim; the Prophet should not obey him but should prostrate and draw near to God through obedience.
rows.anchor:
أي ليس الأمر على ما عليه أبوجهل.
(لا تطعه واسجد واقترب)
أي وتقرب إلى ربك بالطاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the sura is labeled Medinan, the author says the correct view is that it is Meccan.
rows.anchor: مدنية وقيل الصحيح (مكية)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in anzalnāhu refers to the Qur'an, whose prior mention is in 44:1–3, the passage about revelation in a blessed night.
rows.anchor: الهاء ضمير القرآن ولم يجر له ذكر في أول السورة ولكنه جرى ذكره فيما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laylat al-qadr is the night of decree, when every wise matter is distinguished, and the whole Qur'an descended to the lowest heaven before Gabriel revealed it to the Prophet over twenty years.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ليلة القدر ليلة الحكم قال الله تعالى: (فيها يفرق كل أمر حكيم).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is better than a thousand months that do not contain Laylat al-qadr.
rows.anchor: من ألف شهر ليس فيه ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend with what God decrees for the coming year, up to the next Laylat al-qadr.
rows.anchor: تنزل الملائكة بما يقضي الله عز وجل في ليلة القدر للسنة إلى أن تأتي ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A reading min kulli imriʾin is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās; it differs from the muṣḥaf but is transmitted from him.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (من كل امرئ) (1)، وهذه القراءة تخالف المصحف، إلا أنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is peace, free of illness; Satan cannot do evil then, and al-rūḥ is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: أي لا داء فيها، ولا يستطيع الشيطان أن يصنع فيها سيئا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṭlaʿ is read with either fatḥa or kasra on lām: fatḥa gives a verbal noun meaning rising, while kasra denotes the time or place of rising.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (مطلع الفجر)، ومطلع الفجر - بفتح اللام والكسر -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zilzāl is an intense shaking; kasra on zāy is the preferred reading, though fatḥa is allowed in Arabic and has been read.
rows.anchor: إذا حركت حركة شديدة، والقراءة (زلزالها) بكسر الزاي، ويجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth brings out its treasures and its dead.
rows.anchor: أخرجت كنوزها وموتاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human asking what is happening is an unbeliever who did not believe in resurrection and asks why the earth is shaking.
rows.anchor: هذا قول الكافر لأنه لم يكن يؤمن با

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmʾidh is an adverb governed by idhā zullizalat and akhrajat; the earth tells what deeds were done upon it.
rows.anchor: منصوب بقوله: (إذا زلزلت)، وأخرجت، في ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People emerge separated into groups: some did good and others evil.
rows.anchor: أي يصدرون متفرقين منهم من عمل صالحا ومنهم من عمل شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading is transmitted for liyaraw, but the author knows no one who recited it and rejects reciting a merely grammatical possibility without a transmitted reading.
rows.anchor: ويروى (ليروا أعمالهم)، ولا أعلم أحدا قرأ بها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has recorded the servants' good deeds; each person sees his work, and God may forgive or recompense as He wills.
rows.anchor: تأويله أن الله جل وعز قد أحصى أعمال العباد من خير، وكل يرى عمله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says whoever does an atom's weight of good or evil sees it in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقيل من يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره في الدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading ʿumud is a plural of ʿimād or ʿamad, just as ihāb has plural forms ahab and uhb; the pillars are of fire.
rows.anchor: وقرئت (في عمد) وهو جمع عماد وعمد وعمد، كما قالوا: إهاب وأهب وأهب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayfa is the object of faʿala rabbuka, not of alam tara, because kayfa is interrogative; alam tara means did you not know.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب ب (فعل ربك) لا بقوله: (ألم تر)، لأن كيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God informed the Messenger about a past account that demonstrates divine oneness and honors the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ما كان مما سلف من الأقاصيص وما فيه دال على توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Arabs living in Najāshī's land accidentally burned their Christian prayer house by leaving a fire; the wind carried it, and their ruler set out to destroy the Kaaba and seize Mecca.
rows.anchor: فأججوا نارا استعملوها لبعض ما احتاجوا إليه، ثم رحلوا ولم يطفئوها فحملتها الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mounts would not approach the sanctuary but would move when turned back; despite this warning, they persisted, so God sent birds in flocks with three stones each, marked for the man struck and exiting through his body.
rows.anchor: فلما قربوا من الحرم لم تسر بهم دوابهم نحو البيت فإذا عطفوها راجعين سارت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abābīl means groups arriving from here and there; the birds and stones came from every side.
rows.anchor: جماعات من ههنا وجماعات من ههنا والمعنى أرسل الله عليهم هذا الطير بهذه الحجارة من كل جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjīl describes severe punishment and is used of Lot's people in 11:82; Arabs use it for hardship, not agreeable things.
rows.anchor: وصف الله في كل من عذبه بالحجارة أنها من سجيل، فقال في قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poet uses sijīlan for a severe blow in battle, evidencing the word's association with hardship.
rows.anchor: ورجلة يضربون البيض عن عرض. . . ضربا تواصت به الأبطال سجيلا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says abābīl has no singular; other grammarians offer ibālah as a collective noun or ibūl as its singular.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: لا واحد لها، وقال غيره: إبالة وأبابيل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were made like dry, eaten crop leaves, with rot or worms having eaten them.
rows.anchor: أي جعلهم كورق الزرع الذي جف وأكل: أي: وقع فيه الأكال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir reports that God sent a flood which carried them to the sea.
rows.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن الله تعالى أرسل عليهم سيلا فحملهم إلى البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three forms are proposed for the opening: li-īlāfi, li-īlāf, and li-ilfi; the first two are read.
rows.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه: (لإلاف قريش)، و (لإيلاف قريش)، ووجه ثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īlāfihim permits the same forms; this verse has been read ilfihim or īlāfihim, and ilāfihim is also possible.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه قد قرئ في هذها إلفهم " و" إيلافهم " ويجوز إلافهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis connects the lām to the previous sura: the army was destroyed so Quraysh could retain their familiar winter and summer journeys.
rows.anchor: قيل هي موصولة بما قبلها، المعنى فجعلهم كعصف مأكول لإلف قريش.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the lām as an expression of wonder: marvel at Quraysh's established custom.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: هذه لام التعجب فكان المعنى اعجبوا لإيلاف قريش.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred grammatical view connects the lām with the following command: Quraysh should worship the Lord for their familiar journeys.
rows.anchor: وقال النحويون الذين ترتضى عربيتهم: هذه اللام معناها متصل بما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh traveled to Syria in winter and Yemen in summer to provision themselves, safely while others were attacked, claiming sanctuary protection when threatened.
rows.anchor: والتأويل أن قريشا كانوا يرحلون في الشتاء إلى الشام وفي الصيف إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their safety and sustenance despite living in a barren town demonstrate God's oneness; 29:67 contrasts their secure sanctuary with people being snatched away elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فأعلم الله سبحانه أن من الدلالة على وحدانيته ما فعل بهؤلاء لأنهم ببلد لا زرع فيه وأنهم فيه آمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had suffered hardship and eaten carrion; God protected them from fear in the sanctuary and on their journeys.
rows.anchor: وكانوا قد أصابتهم شدة حتى أكلوا الميتة والجيف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aliftu al-makān means I became accustomed to the place; ālaftu is also used with the sense of aliftu.
rows.anchor: ألفت المكان آلفه إلفا، وآلفت المكان بمعنى ألفت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading keeps the second hamza in araʾayta; deleting it is easier at the start of a question, but rītu is not attested from Arabs for رأيت.
rows.anchor: والاختيار أرأيت بإثبات الهمزة الثانية لأن الهمزة إنما طرحت للمستقبل في ترى ويرى وأرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaduʿ means to push, as in being violently pushed into Hell in 52:13; the orphan-denier pushes the orphan away from his rights.
rows.anchor: معنى يدع في اللغة يدفع، وكذلك قوله: (يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is explained as leaving the orphan neglected and not caring for him.
rows.anchor: تأويله فذلك الذي لا يعبأ باليتيم ويتركه مهملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He neither feeds the needy person nor tells others to feed him.
rows.anchor: أي لا يطعم المسكين ولا يأمر بإطعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir describes al-kawthar as a river in Paradise whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, with hollow pearl domes along its banks.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن الكوثر نهر في الجنة أشد بياضا من اللبن وأحلى من العسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another tafsir takes al-kawthar as Islam and prophethood; lexically it is a fawʿal form from abundance, meaning abundant good.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: الكوثر فوعل من الكثرة، ومعناه الخير الكثير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet received all these blessings, including Islam, prophethood, public victory for his religion, victory over enemies, intercession, and innumerable gifts in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وجميع ما جاء في تفسير هذا قد أعطيه النبي عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can mean pray and also slaughter for your Lord; most tafsir identifies the prayer as the Eid prayer followed by sacrifice.
rows.anchor: أي وانحر أيضا لربك، وقيل يعنى به صلاة الغداة في يوم النحر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority interpretation is the prayer on the Day of Sacrifice followed by slaughter; another view has the worshipper fold the right hand over the left at the chest.
rows.anchor:
والأكثر فيما جاء " فصل لربك وانحر "
صلاة يوم الأضحى ثم النحر بعد الصلاة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shāniʾ means hater; the verse answers al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who called the Prophet abtar, cut off without descendants.
rows.anchor: (شانئك) مبغضك وهذا هو العاص بن وائل دخل النبي عليه السلام وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abtar may mean cut off from descendants or deprived of every good; batar means severing completely.
rows.anchor:
فجائز أن يكون هو المنقطع العقب.
وجائز أن يكون هو المنقطع عنه كل خير.
والبتر استئصال القطع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denials apply both now and in the future: the Prophet will not worship what they worship, and they will not worship his God; God has informed him they will not believe.
rows.anchor: أي لست في حالي هذه عابدا ما تعبدون ولا أنتم عابدون ما أعبد ولا أنا عابد ما عبدتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing declaration is said to have preceded the command to fight.
rows.anchor: قيل هذا قبل أن يؤمر - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالقتال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One tafsir says the sura announces the Prophet's death: once Mecca is conquered and people enter Islam in groups, his term is near, and he said the sura had announced his death to him.
rows.anchor: قيل إن الفتح كما جاء في التفسير أنه نعيت إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - نفسه في هذه السورة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God then ordered abundant glorification and seeking forgiveness so the Prophet would end his life by increasing righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: فأمره الله عز وجل أن يكثر التسبيح والاستغفار ليختم له في آخر عمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afwājan means many groups: after people entered singly or in pairs, whole tribes began entering Islam.
rows.anchor:
جماعات كثيرة، أي بعد أن كانوا يدخلون واحدا واحدا.
واثنين اثنين، صارت القبيلة تدخل بأسرها في الإسلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbat yadā means Abū Lahab's hands were ruined or lost.
rows.anchor: معناه خسرت يدا أبي لهب، وتب: أي خسر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir recounts that the Prophet invited his uncles to a meal that miraculously fed them with almost no food missing; when they asked what following him would bring, he said equal Muslim duties and reward, and Abū Lahab cursed him, prompting the sura.
rows.anchor: فأكلوا منها جميعا ولم ينقص منها إلا الشيء اليسير، فقالوا: مالنا عندك إن اتبعناك،

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators say mā kasaba refers to his children; grammatically mā is nominative and the sense is his wealth and what he earned.
rows.anchor: المفسرون قالوا: ما كسب هاهنا ولده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He and his son will enter a flaming fire; another reading is also noted for siyaṣlā.
rows.anchor:
أي: وولده سيصلى نارا ذات لهب.
ويقرأ: (سيصلى نارا).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With wife coordinated to the pronoun in siyaṣlā, the verse says he and his wife will burn, and ḥammālat is her adjective; the accusative can instead be a blame epithet.
rows.anchor: أحدهما العطف على ما في " سيصلى "، المعنى سيصلى هو وامرأته ويكون (حمالة الحطب) نعتا لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-mraʾatuhu may instead be an independent subject, with ḥammālat as its adjective and the rope on her neck as its predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز رفع (وامرأته) على الابتداء، و (حمالة) من نعتها، ويكون الخبر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir identifies the wife as Umm Jamīl, who walked about spreading gossip; an anonymous poem uses walking among people with wet firewood for gossip.
rows.anchor:
وجاء في التفسير.
(حمالة الحطب) أنها أم جميل وأنها كانت تمشي بالنميمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says she carried thorn branches and threw them in the Prophet's and his companions' path.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها كانت تحمل الشوك، شوك العضاة فتطرحه في طريق النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jīd means neck.
rows.anchor: الجيد العنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir says the rope of masad is a chain seventy cubits long, through which she is strung.
rows.anchor:
وقيل في التفسير: (حبل من مسد). سلسلة طولها سبعون ذراعا.
يعنى أنها تسلك في السلسلة سبعون ذراعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, masad is rope of palm fiber, and can also denote ropes made from camel hindquarters; a poem attests the latter usage.
rows.anchor: والمسد في لغة العرب الحبل إذا كان من ليف المقل، وقد يقال لما كان من أدبار الإبل من الحبال مسد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard reading gives aḥad tanwīn; other readings omit it in aḥad Allāh al-ṣamad or leave dāl unvocalized, either to avoid adjacent sukūns or by stopping and restarting.
rows.anchor:
بتنوين أحد، وقرئت بترك التنوين " أحد الله الصمد "
وقرئت بإسكان الدال. وحذف التنوين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huwa refers to God: the one whose identity they asked to know is God; aḥad is nominative in a construction meaning He is one, He is God.
rows.anchor: وأما (هو)، فإنما هو كناية عن ذكر الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively huwa introduces the matter, as in هو زيد قائم, meaning the matter is that God is one.
rows.anchor: " هو " للأمر كما تقول هو زيد قائم، أي الأمر زيد قائم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir says the polytheists asked the Prophet to describe God's lineage, and the response includes that none is His equal.
rows.anchor: روي في التفسير أن المشركين قالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - انسب لنا ربك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣamad is the master at whom sovereignty ends; an anonymous poem uses al-sayyid al-ṣamad for ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: وتفسير (الصمد) السيد الذي ينتهي إليه السؤدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other definitions are the one with no cavity, or the one to whom all things turn, who created everything and is needed by all; these descriptions all fit God and show His oneness.
rows.anchor: وقيل الصمد الذي لا جوف له، وقيل الصمد الذي صمد له كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four readings are given for kafu: with both vowels ḍamma, with ḍamma on kāf and sukūn on fāʾ, with kasra on kāf and sukūn on fāʾ, and kifāʾ with kasra.
rows.anchor: فيها أربعة أوجه في القراءة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafʾ with fatḥa on kāf and sukūn on fāʾ is a noun but is not a reading; another form is impermissible in recitation.
rows.anchor: والكفء - بفتح الكاف وسكون الفاء اسم. لم يقرأ بها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person is said to be another's kufʾ or like his kafaʾ; the chapter also reports a hadith assigning one-third of the Qur'an to al-Ikhlāṣ, one-quarter to al-Kāfirūn, and one-half to al-Zalzalah.
rows.anchor:
ويقال فلان كفء فلان مثل كفي فلان (1).
جاء في الحديث أن (قل هو الله أحد)
تعدل بثلث القرآن، و (قل يا أيها الكافرون) تعدل ربع القرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-falaq is dawn's break and brightness, also called farq al-ṣubḥ; it can mean creation, since splitting produces seed, dawn, plants, and rain, and most creation emerges through splitting.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الفلق الخلق: قال الله عز وجل: (فالق الإصباح)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghāsiq is night and waqaba means it entered; night may be ghāsiq because it is colder than day.
rows.anchor: وقيل لليل غاسق - والله أعلم - لأنه أبرد من النهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-naffāthāt are sorceresses who blow and spit without saliva, as those who perform incantations do.
rows.anchor: (النفاثات) السواحر، تنفث: تتفل بلا ريق كأنه نفخ كما يفعل كل من يرقى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waswās and al-khannās mean the possessor of whispering and retreating; both refer to Satan.
rows.anchor: ذو الوسواس، وذو الخناس وهو الشيطان (الذي يوسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafsir describes Satan with a snake-like head crouching on the heart: when a servant remembers God he withdraws, and when the servant leaves remembrance he returns to whisper.
rows.anchor: وقيل في التفسير: إن له رأس كرأس الحية، يجثم على القلب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view allows al-nās to mean both jinn and humans, so the whispering occurs in the breasts of jinn who are people and of people generally.
rows.anchor:
قيل: الناس هنا يصلح للجن والإنس
المعنى على هذا القول: يوسوس في صدور الناس الذين هم جن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq instead takes the phrase as identifying the whisperers among jinn, then coordinates al-nās with al-waswās to seek refuge from both jinn and human beings.
rows.anchor:
والتأويل عند أبي إسحاق غير هذا
المعنى: " قل أعوذ برب الناس من شر الوسواس الخناس

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He says the prayer seeks refuge from evil jinn and humans, supported by the parallel request for refuge from the evil of what God created.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وهذا المعنى عليه أمر الدعاء، إنه يستعاذ من شر الجن والإنس،
